findings.title: priority.upper() called before null/missing check — AttributeError on absent priority
findings.description: When a caller omits the priority field (or sends null), the parameter arrives as None. The call priority.upper() on line 47 raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'upper'. FastAPI catches this as an unhandled exception and returns HTTP 500. Concrete input: POST /tickets with body {"title": "T"} (no priority). Wrong result: 500 Internal Server Error instead of 400 invalid_priority.
findings.recommendation: Add a null check before normalising: if priority is None: raise ValidationError('invalid_priority', 'priority is required'). Only then call priority.strip().upper().

findings.title: No allowed-value check on priority — any string is accepted and stored
findings.description: After calling .upper() on priority, the code stores the result without checking whether it is one of the allowed values (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH). Any string is accepted. Concrete input: POST /tickets with {"title": "T", "priority": "URGENT"}. Wrong result: 201 Created, ticket stored with priority='URGENT'.
findings.recommendation: After normalising, check membership: if normalised not in ALLOWED_PRIORITIES: raise ValidationError('invalid_priority', 'priority must be one of LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH'). ALLOWED_PRIORITIES is already defined in the module.
